To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ssm4 regulates nuclear movement by regulating microtubular organisation in response to phermone.

(1) S. pombe p150-GlUED Ssm4p associates with the cytoplamic dynein heavy-chain complex and regulates dynein localisation; (2) Ssm4p and the Tip1p homologue of CLIP-170 collaborate to regulate the microtubular cytoskeleton in response to phermone; and (3) Ssm4 is required for nuclear movement during shmooing and meiosis.
Ssm4, a p150-glued homologue, is a novel regulator of nuclear movement in S. pombe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of microtubule-dependent motility in the fission yeast S. pombe.
the mechanisms that regulate the dynamics and organisation of the microtubular cytoskeleton in response to environmental cues.
the role played by Ssm4p in the regulation of microtubule dynamics in fission yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ssm4 is a key regulator of nuclear movement and microtubule dynamics in fission yeast.
our results show that the Ssm4p-Tip1p dynein complex is required to establish the shmooing growth mode and nuclear movement.
the p150-Gluded Ssm4p plays an important role in the regulation of microtubular dynamic and nuclear movement during the sexual development of S. pombe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ssm4 regulates the microtubule dynamics in response to phermone and this in turn affects dynein heavy chains localisation and dynein-dependent nuclear movements.
Ssm4 regulates dynein function in response to mating phermone and that this is essential for the nuclear movements that occur in response to mating and meiosis.
Ssm4 is required to induce the shmooing growth form and that this induction is mediated by the regulation of microtubular nucleation and dynein heavy-chain localisation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p150-Gluded family of proteins has a conserved role in regulating microtubular behaviour during the sexual life cycle of eukaryotes.
Ssm4 is a novel regulator of microtubule dynamics and nuclear movement.
the p150-Glues family member Ssm4p plays an important role in the regulation of microtubular and nuclear dynamics in response to phermone.
